requirement:
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
rationale:
I found no gap in the implementation or the tests for `requirements.authoring.invocation`. The tests all pass the `author` flags through `main`, so they exercise the real command path.

**Obligations and code**
- **Command form and alias.** `src/main.rs#enum[Command]` defines `Author` with `subject`, `--config`, `--missing`, `--force`, `--stdout` and `-v/--verbose`. `--missing` conflicts with `--force` and `--stdout`, and `--all` conflicts with `--stdout`. It also declares `alias = "author-evidence"`. `--config` is passed through as `config.as_deref()`; how it selects a configuration is covered by `requirements.authoring.configuration_precedence`, not by this requirement.
- **Authoring one existing requirement or named example.** `src/main.rs#fn[main]` calls `author_evidence_with_options`. Its `AuthoringSubject::parse` (in `src/authoring/mod.rs`) yields `Definition(name)`. `configured_record` then calls `subject.sources(root)`, which reaches `AssessmentSources::prepare` in `src/authoring/inputs.rs`. `prepare` rejects any name that is not a requirement or example with "no matching requirement or named example".
- **Applying `requirements.authoring.refresh`.** `author_evidence_with_options` treats `--stdout` as `--force`. Otherwise it returns `None` when `batch::subject_is_current` says the evidence is current, before any configuration is resolved. `main` reports this case as "evidence is current; 1 skipped as current".
- **Completion report.** `main` prints `subject: backend / model; policy`, then `Evidence: <path>` and `Usage: <path>`. `AuthoringOutcome` carries the subject, backend, model, `evidence_path` and `usage_path`.
- **Evidence destination.** `configured_assessment` returns `Some(path)` for `EvidenceOutput::File` and `None` for `Stdout`. `main` prints the evidence path in the first case and `Evidence: stdout` in the second.
- **Stdout mode.** The evidence JSON is the only thing written to stdout. The completion report, the false-judgment line and rationale, and coverage-loss failures use `eprintln!`. Coverage-loss reviews are only printed to stdout when there are any, and none arise in stdout mode because `replaced` is only filled in file mode.

**Tests**
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject]` is marked `{test}` for this requirement. It covers the `author-evidence` alias, `--missing` and `--force` conflicts, `--stdout` implying `--force`, and current records being kept even when the config file is unusable.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` runs `author-evidence`. It asserts the report starts with `SUBJECT: ollama / MODEL` and that the `Evidence:` path ends in `evidence/<subject>.json`. It also asserts the `Usage:` line.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` asserts stdout is only the JSON. It asserts stderr has the report, `Evidence: stdout` and the usage path, and that the rationale appears in stderr only for a false judgment under verbose.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[verbose_single_author_reports_only_false_rationale_without_source_inputs]` covers `-v` and `--verbose`.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[author_rejects_unknown_subjects_and_conflicting_targets]` covers a nonexistent subject and the clap conflicts.
- The `Fixture` struct and its `run` and `command` helpers carry `{test}` references.

No `{fixme}` references are involved.

text: :::{req} invocation
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
:::{req} refresh
Every `habeas author` form MUST accept `--missing` and `--force`, which are
mutually exclusive; `--missing` MUST be the default. Under `--missing`, the
command MUST assess only the selected subjects whose evidence is missing, stale,
or invalid, and MUST preserve every current record without invoking a model,
including accepted FIXME judgments and current false judgments; a current false
judgment is reassessed only when its subject or inputs change or `--force` is
given. Under `--force`, the command MUST assess every selected subject. `--stdout`
MUST imply `--force`, because it writes no evidence. The command MUST report the
number of selected subjects it skipped as current. When no assessment is needed,
the command MUST succeed without resolving model configuration or credentials.
